topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, learning objectives, and progression model for understanding cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and proliferative mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how oncogenic mutations in cell surface receptor pathways drive sustained proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: They illustrate how developmental blocks preventing terminal differentiation contribute to malignant transformation in blood and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It examines how alterations in p53 and mitochondrial apoptotic regulators enable cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomeres, senescence, and p53-mediated stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the mechanisms governing cellular lifespan limits, telomerase reactivation, and p53-mediated responses to cellular stress before summarizing cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and oncometabolite-driven oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how cancer cells rewire their metabolic networks and how metabolic enzyme mutations act as drivers of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It addresses how developing tumors overcome oxygen diffusion limits by triggering new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the complete metastatic cascade from vascular dissemination and tissue colonization to genomic characteristics and clinical monitoring.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing reflections on hallmark integration and offers final logistical guidance for the course.
